title: Choose the visual world for PAM's console
question: The roll assigned the Hisaab Register. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Hisaab Register
options.lineage: the ruled hisaab/khata notebook every Indian household and kirana shop keeps
options.thesis: Your month as one ruled register page: dates in the red margin, rupees and paise in their own columns, transfers written as Contra and struck out of spend.
options.viewport: One folio for the selected month: true-spend total written in ink at the head with the naive ledger figure struck through beside it, budget lines ruled under each category, and a red-margin date column running down the entry list.
options.risk: If the paper metaphor is rendered literally (texture, handwriting fonts) it turns twee; it only works as ruling, columns and ink states.

raised.raise: Nothing disappears, it cancels: reversals, deleted and superseded entries stay on the page struck through with their reason stamped.
One ruling discipline: every rule, budget line and focus bracket drawn at one device pixel from the same three inks; states are printed marks, not glows.
Rows are live entities and columns never move: a job or exception changes state by restyling its row in place.

options.label: Bank Passbook
options.lineage: printed savings passbooks updated at the branch kiosk
options.thesis: Each account a passbook: dot-matrix entries, withdrawal / deposit / balance columns, the branch stamp on reconciled months.
options.viewport: Account passbook spread with balance column and month stamp; budgets on the facing page.
options.risk: The familiar banking look most finance apps already wear; it shows accounts well but hides budgets and transfers.

options.label: Centre-rail Reference
options.lineage: wide-margin reference editions set by a ruling engine
options.thesis: Debits and credits as twin columns around a vermilion rail of dates.
options.viewport: Two dense columns round a date rail, notes in the margin.
options.case: Clear for accountants, foreign to households; loses audience identification and scanability.
options.risk: Literary density slows a customer checking one number.
options.kept: One-device-pixel ruling discipline and states as printed marks.

options.label: Jet-age Ticket Wallet
options.thesis: Recurring bills as coupons torn off month by month.
options.viewport: A coupon book of this month's bills.
options.case: Nice for recurring payments only; travel ephemera is not this audience's money world.
options.risk: Breaks down for budgets and analyst queues.

options.label: Split-flap Concourse
options.thesis: Bills and jobs as departures on a flap board.
options.viewport: Upcoming bills as a departures board.
options.case: Fits the admin job queue, not a household's month; loses both axes for customers.
options.kept: Rows are live entities; columns never move.

options.label: Labanotation Score
options.thesis: Length encodes exact quantity on a vertical staff.
options.viewport: Month as a rising staff of spend blocks.
options.case: Unreadable to households; loses both axes.
options.kept: Bar length is exact: budget and spend bars share one true scale.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A clean fintech dashboard: stat cards, charts, sidebar, executed impeccably.
canonCard.viewport: Stat cards row, budget bar chart, recent transactions table.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from every finance dashboard by design.
